Tier-1 event index: the antecedent rain index behind the matching gate

Source: R/reference_model.R
dot-tier1_event_index.Rd

The single definition of the hydrological index that tier-1 direct matching compares. It is used for all three quantities in the gate – the index stored on each reference observation (obs$hydro_event), the target date's index, and the IQR-based default tolerance match_hydro_tol – so that the comparison and its tolerance are on one scale. .compute_api() is an un-normalised store whose level grows roughly with tau, so mixing taus (as the gate once did: a 30-d store against a 5-d one, gated by the spread of a 1-d one) leaves same-day, same-rain pairs tens of mm apart and tier 1 practically never fires.

Usage

.tier1_event_index(hydro_values, hydro_dates, target_dates, match_window_days)

Arguments

hydro_values, hydro_dates

Daily hydrology series.

target_dates

Date vector; the index is evaluated at each.

match_window_days

Tier-1 time window (days).

Value

Numeric vector, same length as target_dates.

Details

The memory constant is match_window_days: the gate asks whether the rain over roughly the matching window differs between the two dates, which is the time scale on which a grab within that window is a valid proxy. It is floored at 1 day so match_window_days = 0 (same-day matches only) still yields a valid reservoir.
